data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新型橡胶材料的潜在影响和应用

不同观点：
• **sans_souse** 认为，这种新型橡胶材料有巨大的应用潜力。他指出，这种材料在被切割后不仅不会撕裂，还能继续承重，解决了传统橡胶作为基材时的一个主要缺点。这可能在多个应用场景中带来革命性变化。他对此消息表示感谢。

• **elihu** 关注这种新材料在轮胎制造中的潜在应用，尤其是对环境的影响。他提到，现代轮胎约1/3由天然橡胶制成，如果能够使用接近100%的天然橡胶，可能会减少轮胎磨损产生的微塑料污染。然而，他也指出，天然橡胶的需求量可能会增加三倍，这在实际生产中可能不现实。此外，他还提到了纯橡胶轮胎的耐磨性问题，如果纯橡胶轮胎磨损更快，那么需求量会进一步增加；但如果磨损更慢，当前的生产量可能就足够了。他还补充，电动汽车由于重量更大，轮胎磨损更快，这也需要考虑。

补充讨论：
• **teleforce** 提供了一个相关的新闻来源，提到哈佛大学的一个突破性研究，改进了橡胶的抗裂性能，使其强度提高了10倍。这为讨论提供了一个科学依据，并指向了具体的研究来源，增加了讨论的学术性和可信度。

争议焦点：
• 天然橡胶在轮胎中的应用潜力与现实生产能力之间的矛盾。一方面，使用天然橡胶可以减少微塑料污染，但另一方面，天然橡胶的需求量大幅增加可能不现实，且耐磨性问题也需要进一步研究。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在创作《Dust 2》续作时的思考过程和设计理念。尽管《Dust》非常成功，但制作续作《Dust 3》仍然是一个艰巨的任务。作者希望新地图既保留《Dust》的精髓，又不完全是其复制品。关键元素如拱门、石路和装饰线条被精心保留和调整，以维持地图的独特风格和玩法平衡。同时，新元素如半螺旋楼梯和岩石面的加入为玩家提供了新的挑战。最终，作者通过细致调整地图布局，确保新地图既有新鲜感，又不失原作的节奏和平衡。

44303715.article_content:
Introduction
Despite the success and overwhelming popularity of Dust, the thought of making a sequel took a long time to cross my mind. Although considered by some to be it’s spiritual successor, Cobble failed to find the same audience, and there was clear demand for a ‘real’ sequel. Dust 2 didn’t arrive until March 2001 - nearly 2 years after the original.
It was never going to be easy creating a successor to the most-played FPS map in the world. Even with the benefit of the same texture set, an established theme and innumerable number of salivating CS players, it was an incredibly daunting task. I didn’t want to call it “Dust 2” for this very reason. Instead, on the basis that the third instalment of any movie trilogy is typically never as good as the first one, I decided to call it “Dust 3”, and hoped no-one would notice. My assumption was that everyone would just carry on playing the original.
So, I opened up Hammer, and started laying out “Dust 3”.
Sticking to a Theme
First things first, I had to ensure that this new map had everything in common with Dust, without actually
being
Dust. I had to identify the elements that defined a Dust map.
The Arches
Perhaps the most iconic aspect of Dust are the arches that separate main gameplay areas. Aesthetically they neatly compartmentalise the map, framing entrances and exits between areas and helping players create a mental picture of the layout. From a gameplay perspective, they produce tight choke-points between objectives, and block out unwanted lines-of-sight. Consider how Dust would have looked without the arches:
Lose the arches and you get a deathmatch arena.
It’s worth reading the original
Making of Dust
if you haven’t already, as you’ll see the arches (amongst many other elements) were lifted directly from Team Fortress 2.
The Road
The stone roads through Dust were like arteries, giving players clear paths to follow towards the main objective areas. The sequel would do the same, connecting spawn points to the primary objectives.
As an example of the importance of these paths, here’s what Dust would have looked like without them:
Where we're going, we really do need 'roads'.
The Trim
The much-abused ‘trim’ along all the walls and ceilings of Dust was perhaps the single element that gave the world a hint of relief and purpose, and helped separate distinct geometric elements. It was incredibly important in a world that was almost otherwise entirely made of the same colour stone.
I therefore tried to use the trim very carefully, only exactly where needed, and not just as filler. I didn’t want to repeat the mistake of many Dust-alikes where it had been peppered everywhere it fitted, flooding the visual cortex of players with the excessive complexity. Neither did I want to under-employ it, and end up with a world looking flat and barren.
I tried to formalise the rules I’d employed. The trim would never appear on a floor or ceiling, or anywhere a player could stand on it. It would never be striped or tiled vertically across a surface. Finally, for any given flat wall, it would never appear more than twice (e.g. at the top, and at the bottom, but never in the middle as well.)
The Sun
This was perhaps the element of Dust that underwent the most tweaking - every BETA release of Counter-Strike saw it moved ever so slightly, lengthening the shadows each time. It was key to making Dust distinct amongst the other maps in rotation, and keeping it accessible and pleasant to play in. I considered giving the sequel a night setting, but in doing so would have removed a vital element of the Dust theme. The best I could do was make it exactly the same.
The Design
This new Dust had to bear resemblance to the original beyond the texture set and sunlight. It had to copy important design elements that players had become accustomed to: the ‘Dust doors’, simple structures, ramps, crates and arbitrarily raised concrete areas. In fact, I’d have to copy some areas nearly verbatim to ensure the lineage was present.
At the same time, while trying to differentiate the sequel from the original, I’d have to be conservative about any
new
elements I was introducing. These came in the form of the half-spiral staircase, and the rock face adjoining the two bomb spot areas.
There were also two distinct boxes that Dust 3 needed to tick - a place for close-quarters battles, and a place for long, drawn-out AWP fights. Dust had the central corridor and the underpass to fulfil these requirements, and I’d have to create something similar in the sequel to cater for both types of player.
It was a lot to juggle.
Keeping It Simple
Of course, the most important element that would make or break the sequel was the overall map layout. It had to be Dust-ish, without being Dust, different enough to give players a fresh challenge, but maintaining the balance and pace of the original.

data.author: beigebrucewayne

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI生成内容、LLM（大语言模型）工具（如Claude Code）的使用体验、可靠性及其对开发流程的影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• **对AI生成内容的质量存在质疑**：mjrbrannan认为AI生成的总结质量差，内容空洞，像糟糕的公关文，不如直接查看代码提交记录有效。blahgeek进一步指出，像解释Rust借阅检查器这样的任务对LLM来说并不难，因为这类数据在训练集中很常见。

• **LLM工具在开发中的应用价值**：jumski和SamPatt对Claude Code持积极态度，认为它不仅在代码相关任务上表现出色，还能用于其他多种工作流，比如自动化任务和文档管理。Syzygies则强调不同模型之间的差异，指出高阶模型在特定任务（如数学研究）中的重要性。

• **LLM工具对开发流程和团队习惯的长期影响**：b0a04gl关注模型生成的代码对团队代码审查习惯和长期质量的影响，担心模型可能降低代码变更的严谨性。tinyhouse则认为文章中提到的很多功能并非新事物，质疑文章将普通自动化与AGI（通用人工智能）混为一谈。

• **LLM的法律和伦理问题**：bionhoward对Anthropic的法律条款表示担忧，认为其限制不合理，质疑其是否能被信任为负责任的技术提供者。

Writing in the Age of LLMs
Table of Contents
In the last couple of years, I’ve written and reviewed several technical papers and blog posts. I often come across LLM-generated writing that feels slightly “off”—sometimes, to be honest, even uninviting. At the same time, I get tremendous value from using LLMs to draft early versions, summarize dense material, and rephrase messy thoughts.
This post details some of my thoughts on writing in a world where much of what we read is now machine-generated. First, I’ll lay out some common patterns of bad writing I see from LLM tools. Then, I’ll defend some writing habits that people often dismiss as “LLM-sounding” but are actually fine—even helpful—when used intentionally. Finally, I’ll share concrete rules and formulas I rely on in my own writing and in the prompts I use to guide LLMs.
Common Patterns of Bad Writing I See from LLM Tools
Here are the red flags I keep seeing—mostly from LLMs, but I suppose also from people trying to sound polished and “formal” in the wrong ways.
Empty “summary” sentences that pretend to conclude a thought
These often show up at the end of a paragraph and sound like:
“By following these steps, we achieve better performance."
"By internalizing these principles, you can cut through the noise.”
Empty summary sentences feel conclusive, but say nothing. I try to end with parting thoughts that offer something new—or at least something to chew on—but unfortunately, I haven’t found a reliable recipe for getting LLMs to write with that kind of substance.
Overuse of bullet points and outlines
LLMs often overuse bullet points, especially nested ones. Lists help when items are parallel and independent, but when ideas are connected or need context, a paragraph is usually better.
Flat sentence rhythm
When every sentence is the same length, the writing lacks rhythm and becomes harder to follow. Varied sentence lengths keep readers engaged. They help signal emphasis, guide attention, and control the pace.
Bad example:
We recently launched a conversational AI feature that lets users ask questions in plain English and get responses based on their past activity and current session. The system searches a database of help articles, ranks the most relevant ones using a custom scoring function, and passes the top result into a language model to generate the final answer. We spent weeks optimizing each step to keep latency under 300 milliseconds, including caching, pruning irrelevant articles, and tuning prompt templates.
Good example:
We just launched a new conversational AI feature. It answers user questions in plain language, using context from the current session. The system searches help articles, scores them with a custom ranking function, feeds the top result into a fine-tuned language model, and runs in under 300ms using caching, pruning, and prompt tuning techniques.
Not the right subject
Every sentence has a subject and a predicate. The subject tells us what the sentence is about; the predicate tells us what the subject is doing or what’s being said about it. Choosing the right subject helps keep the reader focused on the main idea. A common issue in LLM-generated writing is that it often picks the wrong subject. Consider two variations of the previous sentence:
Bad example:
Readers are better guided when the subject matches the main idea of the sentence.
Good example:
Choosing the right subject keeps the writing clear and focused.
In the bad version, the subject is readers, even though the sentence is about sentence structure, not people. The good version keeps the subject aligned with the topic, making the writing more coherent and easier to follow.
Low information density

As someone who writes, reviews, and deconstructs complex information for a living, I’ve developed a strong allergy to bad writing. And lately, a lot of that bad writing has a specific, synthetic flavor—the unmistakable scent of an LLM. This post is a guide to navigating the new world of writing, with or without LLM assistance. First, I’ll cover the true pitfalls of LLM-generated text—the red flags that make it feel sterile and unconvincing.
It sounds nice but says very little. The sentences are well-formed, but there’s no concrete insight, no framing, no momentum.
Vagueness
LLM writing often avoids specificity. It refers to ideas without defining them and makes claims without evidence. E.g.,
“Some experts say prompt engineering is becoming less important. The ability to simply prompt LLMs can have a major impact on productivity.”
But who are the experts? What exactly is the impact? On what kind of work, and for whom? Without concrete references or clear stakes, the writing feels vague and insubstantial.

data.title: Breaking Quadratic Barriers: A Non-Attention LLM for Ultra-Long Context Horizons
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种不依赖注意力机制的大语言模型（LLM）架构，能够高效处理超长上下文，范围可达数十万至数百万 tokens。与传统Transformer的二次计算和内存需求不同，该模型通过结合状态空间块（State Space blocks）、多分辨率卷积层（Multi Resolution Convolution layers）、轻量级递归监督器（Recurrent Supervisor）和检索增强外部记忆（Retrieval Augmented External Memory）等组件，避免了token间的注意力计算，实现了近线性扩展。该模型有效解决了长序列处理中的二次瓶颈问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对DeepSeek LLM及其相关研究的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• [albertzeyer] 认为论文中的方法在当前LLM领域并不新颖，尤其是关于自注意力复杂度O(n^2)的解决方案已有大量研究。他指出论文实验部分不足，缺乏对长度外推、大规模实验等关键方面的研究，且实验结果显示的改进较小。此外，他提到矩阵乘法在前馈层的复杂度通常会比自注意力部分更高，因此自注意力部分并非最大问题。

• [maxrmk] 对论文中将DeepSeek架构描述为仍未完全明了的观点提出异议，指出DeepSeek的架构已有详细文档和多种实现，不应该被描述为谜团。

• [yorwba] 认为论文结构不清晰，重复描述架构但缺乏关键细节，例如如何为“外部检索内存”计算梯度。此外，对DeepSeek部分的描述显得故弄玄虚，尽管已有相关论文发表，不需要猜测其是否涉及注意力机制。

• [juank10] 提到代码库中的代码被删除但仍能在提交记录中看到，并推荐了一些当前最先进的非注意力LLM模型（如MesaNet、Rodimus等）。他认为注意力机制在某些任务中仍然不可或缺，尤其是在代码、数学、推理和多轮QA任务中。

• [daxfohl] 提出与LLM计算成本相关的问题，关注按token收费的可持续性，尤其是在计算需求呈二次增长的情况下。

• [imranq] 对去除自注意力复杂度的想法表示赞赏，但认为论文的实验支持不足，缺乏在推理、检索QA、摘要质量等方面的测试，且在困惑度上的改进也较小。不过，他认为非注意力模型的研究空间值得关注。

• [ljlolel] 简单表达了对更多图表的需求。

• [zoklet-enjoyer] 表示对技术细节不了解，但对可能性感到兴奋。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是论文的实验部分不足，尤其是缺乏对关键任务的实验验证。
• 对DeepSeek架构的描述被批评为不必要的神秘化，与其已有详细文档和实现的事实不符。
• 非注意力LLM模型的性能和应用场景也是一个讨论热点，尤其是其在特定任务中的表现和潜力。
• 计算成本和按token收费的可持续性问题也被提及，反映了对LLM商业模式的关注。

总的来说，评论主要围绕论文的创新性、实验设计的不足、以及非注意力模型的潜力和挑战展开讨论。

Abstract:
We present a novel non attention based architecture for large language models (LLMs) that efficiently handles very long context windows, on the order of hundreds of thousands to potentially millions of tokens. Unlike traditional Transformer designs, which suffer from quadratic memory and computation overload due to the nature of the self attention mechanism, our model avoids token to token attention entirely. Instead, it combines the following complementary components: State Space blocks (inspired by S4) that learn continuous time convolution kernels and scale near linearly with sequence length, Multi Resolution Convolution layers that capture local context at different dilation levels, a lightweight Recurrent Supervisor to maintain a global hidden state across sequential chunks, and Retrieval Augmented External Memory that stores and retrieves high-level chunk embeddings without reintroducing quadratic operations.

44292601.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种不依赖注意力机制的大语言模型（LLM）架构，能够高效处理超长上下文，范围可达数十万至数百万 tokens。与传统Transformer的二次计算和内存需求不同，该模型通过结合状态空间块（State Space blocks）、多分辨率卷积层（Multi Resolution Convolution layers）、轻量级递归监督器（Recurrent Supervisor）和检索增强外部记忆（Retrieval Augmented External Memory）等组件，避免了token间的注意力计算，实现了近线性扩展。该模型有效解决了长序列处理中的二次瓶颈问题。
44292601.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对DeepSeek LLM及其相关研究的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• [albertzeyer] 认为论文中的方法在当前LLM领域并不新颖，尤其是关于自注意力复杂度O(n^2)的解决方案已有大量研究。他指出论文实验部分不足，缺乏对长度外推、大规模实验等关键方面的研究，且实验结果显示的改进较小。此外，他提到矩阵乘法在前馈层的复杂度通常会比自注意力部分更高，因此自注意力部分并非最大问题。

• [maxrmk] 对论文中将DeepSeek架构描述为仍未完全明了的观点提出异议，指出DeepSeek的架构已有详细文档和多种实现，不应该被描述为谜团。

• [yorwba] 认为论文结构不清晰，重复描述架构但缺乏关键细节，例如如何为“外部检索内存”计算梯度。此外，对DeepSeek部分的描述显得故弄玄虚，尽管已有相关论文发表，不需要猜测其是否涉及注意力机制。

• [juank10] 提到代码库中的代码被删除但仍能在提交记录中看到，并推荐了一些当前最先进的非注意力LLM模型（如MesaNet、Rodimus等）。他认为注意力机制在某些任务中仍然不可或缺，尤其是在代码、数学、推理和多轮QA任务中。

• [daxfohl] 提出与LLM计算成本相关的问题，关注按token收费的可持续性，尤其是在计算需求呈二次增长的情况下。

• [imranq] 对去除自注意力复杂度的想法表示赞赏，但认为论文的实验支持不足，缺乏在推理、检索QA、摘要质量等方面的测试，且在困惑度上的改进也较小。不过，他认为非注意力模型的研究空间值得关注。

• [ljlolel] 简单表达了对更多图表的需求。

• [zoklet-enjoyer] 表示对技术细节不了解，但对可能性感到兴奋。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是论文的实验部分不足，尤其是缺乏对关键任务的实验验证。
• 对DeepSeek架构的描述被批评为不必要的神秘化，与其已有详细文档和实现的事实不符。
• 非注意力LLM模型的性能和应用场景也是一个讨论热点，尤其是其在特定任务中的表现和潜力。
• 计算成本和按token收费的可持续性问题也被提及，反映了对LLM商业模式的关注。

总的来说，评论主要围绕论文的创新性、实验设计的不足、以及非注意力模型的潜力和挑战展开讨论。

data.title: Nanonets-OCR-s – OCR model that transforms documents into structured markdown
data.author: PixelPanda
data.article_summary: Nanonets-OCR-s是一款先进的图像到Markdown OCR模型，能够将文档转化为结构化的Markdown格式，并具备智能内容识别和语义标记功能，特别适合大型语言模型（LLMs）的后续处理。其主要功能包括：LaTeX公式识别、智能图像描述、签名检测与隔离、水印提取、智能复选框处理以及复杂表格提取。该模型通过提供特定的提示和模板，能够准确提取并格式化文档中的文本、公式、图像、水印、复选框和表格，输出为易于处理的结构化数据。用户可以通过Hugging Face或vLLM等平台使用该模型进行OCR处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nanonets-OCR-s模型的功能、性能、应用场景及其局限性

不同观点：
• PixelPanda：作为Nanonets的员工，分享了Nanonets-OCR-s模型的功能，包括LaTeX公式识别、图像描述、签名检测、水印提取、智能处理复选框和复杂表格提取等。模型轻量且强大，适用于文档结构和内容上下文的解析。
• kordlessagain：尝试在本地运行该模型，但由于老旧GPU（Nvidia 1080 8GB）导致速度很慢，每页需要至少5分钟。并提到正在开发一个基于Cloud Run（支持GPU）的PDF转Markdown工具。
• el_don_almighty：认为该模型是将其十年旧文档转换为标准化格式的重要工具，但还需要一个能够归档和轻松提取元素的功能。
• temp0826：正尝试将Shipibo到西班牙语的字典转换为Shipibo到英语字典，遇到格式和扫描质量问题，可能需要尝试该模型。
• ks2048：质疑这些模型为何只支持Markdown，而不是更具结构化和规范的格式，如支持脚注、参考文献、图表等的格式。
• mvac：询问该模型与Datalab/Marker的比较，他们评估了许多PDF转Markdown工具，Datalab/Marker表现最佳。
• ZQ-Dev8：询问该模型与docling的比较。
• silversmith：对非英语文本的处理能力表示关注，认为基于LLM的OCR解决方案在处理其他语言时表现较差。
• raus22：指出如果模型不提及多语言支持，在实际的非英语PDF上表现会非常差。
• progval：指出该模型并非开源或开放权重。
• jwr：对使用小模型表示好奇，认为大模型（如27B）在处理多语言和减少错误方面表现更好。
• Bestora：询问模型如何处理多列多行表格。
• nehalem：询问模型如何处理多列文本以及页眉页脚。
• tensor：询问是否有基准测试或准确性评估。

补充讨论：
• b0a04gl：对模型在解析时标记语义的功能表示兴趣，认为在布局重建之前识别签名、水印、复选框等是创新的，并好奇这种预标记对下游简化的影响，尤其是转换为json/html时。

争议焦点：
• 模型对非英语文本的处理能力及其多语言支持。
• 模型为何只支持Markdown，而不是更具结构化的格式。
• 模型的开源性和开放权重问题。
• 模型的性能和与其他工具的比较。

44287043.article_content: Nanonets-OCR-s is a powerful, state-of-the-art image-to-markdown OCR model that goes far beyond traditional text extraction. It transforms documents into structured markdown with intelligent content recognition and semantic tagging, making it ideal for downstream processing by Large Language Models (LLMs). Nanonets-OCR-s is packed with features designed to handle complex documents with ease: LaTeX Equation Recognition: Automatically converts mathematical equations and formulas into properly formatted LaTeX syntax. It distinguishes between inline ( $...$ ) and display ( $$...$$ ) equations. Intelligent Image Description: Describes images within documents using structured tags, making them digestible for LLM processing. It can describe various image types, including logos, charts, graphs and so on, detailing their content, style, and context. Signature Detection & Isolation: Identifies and isolates signatures from other text, outputting them within a tag. This is crucial for processing legal and business documents. Watermark Extraction: Detects and extracts watermark text from documents, placing it within a tag. Smart Checkbox Handling: Converts form checkboxes and radio buttons into standardized Unicode symbols ( ☐ , ☑ , ☒ ) for consistent and reliable processing. Complex Table Extraction: Accurately extracts complex tables from documents and converts them into both markdown and HTML table formats. 📢 Read the full announcement | 🤗 Hugging Face Space Demo Usage Using transformers from PIL import Image from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoProcessor, AutoModelForImageTextToText model_path = "nanonets/Nanonets-OCR-s" model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained( model_path, torch_dtype= "auto" , device_map= "auto" , attn_implementation= "flash_attention_2" ) model. eval () tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path) processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_path) def ocr_page_with_nanonets_s ( image_path, model, processor, max_new_tokens= 4096 ): prompt = """Extract the text from the above document as if you were reading it naturally. Return the tables in html format. Return the equations in LaTeX representation. If there is an image in the document and image caption is not present, add a small description of the image inside the tag; otherwise, add the image caption inside . Watermarks should be wrapped in brackets. Ex: OFFICIAL COPY. Page numbers should be wrapped in brackets. Ex: 14 or 9/22. Prefer using ☐ and ☑ for check boxes.""" image = Image. open (image_path) messages = [ { "role" : "system" , "content" : "You are a helpful assistant." }, { "role" : "user" , "content" : [ { "type" : "image" , "image" : f"file:// {image_path} " }, { "type" : "text" , "text" : prompt}, ]}, ] text = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize= False , add_generation_prompt= True ) inputs = processor(text=[text], images=[image], padding= True , return_tensors= "pt" ) inputs = inputs.to(model.device) output_ids = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, do_sample= False ) generated_ids = [output_ids[ len (input_ids):] for input_ids, output_ids in zip (inputs.input_ids, output_ids)] output_text = processor.batch_decode(generated_ids, skip_special_tokens= True , clean_up_tokenization_spaces= True ) return output_text[ 0 ] image_path = "/path/to/your/document.jpg" result = ocr_page_with_nanonets_s(image_path, model, processor, max_new_tokens= 15000 ) print (result) Using vLLM Start the vLLM server. vllm serve nanonets/Nanonets-OCR-s Predict with the model from openai import OpenAI import base64 client = OpenAI(api_key= "123" , base_url= "http://localhost:8000/v1" ) model = "nanonets/Nanonets-OCR-s" def encode_image ( image_path ): with open (image_path, "rb" ) as image_file: return base64.b64encode(image_file.read()).decode( "utf-8" ) def ocr_page_with_nanonets_s ( img_base64 ): response = client.chat.completions.create( model=model, messages=[ { "role" : "user" , "content" : [ { "type" : "image_url" , "image_url" : { "url" : f"data:image/png;base64, {img_base64} " }, }, { "type" : "text" , "text" : "Extract the text from the above document as if you were reading it naturally. Return the tables in html format. Return the equations in LaTeX representation. If there is an image in the document and image caption is not present, add a small description of the image inside the tag; otherwise, add the image caption inside . Watermarks should be wrapped in brackets. Ex: OFFICIAL COPY. Page numbers should be wrapped in brackets. Ex: 14 or 9/22. Prefer using ☐ and ☑ for check boxes." , }, ], } ], temperature= 0.0 , max_tokens= 15000 ) return response.choices[ 0 ].message.content test_img_path = "/path/to/your/document.jpg" img_base64 = encode_image(test_img_path)

data.title: Retrobootstrapping Rust for some reason
data.author: romac
data.article_summary: 本文介绍用户在访问网站时被随机选中进行CAPTCHA验证的步骤。用户需完成验证以继续请求。页面提供登录选项，包括输入账户名和密码，以及"记住我"功能。此外，还有找回密码和使用OpenID登录的选项。用户需完成CAPTCHA验证才能进行登录操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：重现旧软件构建过程中的挑战及解决方案，特别是涉及LLVM、Rust等编译器和编程语言的演变及其对代码兼容性和构建稳定性的影响。

不同观点：
• [kimixa] 认为现代的clang和gcc无法编译旧版本的LLVM，主要因为C++标准的变化。通过在编译选项中添加"std=xxx"可以部分解决该问题。此外，指出C++对旧代码的兼容性支持虽然有利于向后兼容，但也可能对当前版本产生不利影响。
• [jasonthorsness] 对即便在2011年之后的构建步骤难以重现表示担忧，并质疑未来技术是否会变得更加不稳定，担心最终会出现无法重现或重建的技术。
• [LegionMammal978] 分享了自己在Ubuntu 20.04上进行类似项目的经验，遇到了LLVM堆栈问题和缺失的公共repo，指出重建历史提交需要大量努力。
• [tmtvl] 提到Guix在引导Rust时也遇到了类似问题，并引用了一篇2018年的文章来说明该问题。
• [neilv] 提出是否可能创建一个简化的Rust编译器，只接受正确的输入并将其翻译为非检查的C代码，以实现可持续的引导过程。此外，通过引用Debian的例子，强调其对旧软件包的长期支持。
• [gregorvand] 和 [fcoury] 讨论了访问文章时遇到的403错误问题，并提供了替代链接以解决访问问题。
• [15155] 猜测通过更新CA证书和known_hosts文件可以解决与GitHub通信相关的问题。
• [eptcyka] 批评了Nix evangelists的过度推崇，但在该问题上认为使用Nix可以通过固定nixpkgs版本和源代码来实现可重现的引导，减轻未来重现的负担。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是C++标准变化对旧代码兼容性的影响，以及这种兼容性对开发过程的利弊。
• 另一个讨论点是技术演进中的不稳定性及其对未来重现和构建过程的影响。
• 还提到了通过特定工具（如Nix或Guix）来实现可重现构建的可能性和优势。
• 最后，访问某些资源时遇到的实际技术问题（如403错误）也被提出并解决。
